title: Trade journal follow-ups from PR #150 review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #150 (frontend-trade-journal), recorded here so they aren't lost once the PR merges and the review comment scrolls out of view.

checklist.step: frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/TradeJournalPanel.tsx's GradeCell bolds a grade at exactly the threshold (`gradePct >= goodThresholdPct`), but both the grade's own MetricHelp copy ('Elder considers a sell/buy grade over 50% "very good"') and backend/app/api/schemas.py's docstring describe the buy/sell-grade cutoff as strictly '>50%', not '>=50%'. A grade of exactly 50.0% renders bold (visually 'good') while the popover text it sits next to says 'over 50%' -- a genuine off-by-boundary mismatch, narrow edge case but worth aligning (either use a strict `>` comparison for the two 50%-anchored grades, or reword the copy to '50% or more').

components/common/SignedCurrency/SignedCurrency.tsx duplicates the exact sign-to-color three-way ternary (success/error/secondary) and the leading '+' construction already implemented in common/PercentChange -- worth extracting a small shared helper (e.g. a `signColor(value)` utility) so a future change to the app's gain/loss color convention only needs updating in one place, and so a third signed-value component doesn't copy-paste a third time.

TradeJournalPanel.tsx marks buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct as not sortable, with a comment claiming 'DataTable's generic comparator has no defined ordering for a nullable percentage' -- but DataTable.tsx's own compareForSort already defines null-sorts-last behavior for exactly this case (nulls always sort after real values, per its own docstring), mirroring the same (also outdated) rationale already on PositionsTable.tsx's current_price column. These grade columns' underlying values are plain nullable numbers, so they could be marked sortable like the table's other nullable numeric columns -- worth revisiting both this column and the pre-existing PositionsTable precedent it copied.

decisions.decision: Fixed the 50% boundary mismatch by making GradeCell's Buy Grade/Sell Grade columns use a strict `>` comparison (`strictlyAbove` prop, default false) instead of rewording the MetricHelp/backend copy from 'over 50%' to '50% or more'.
decisions.rationale: The copy ('over 50%') already matches Elder's own wording and the backend schemas.py docstring exactly (both use '>50%'); changing the comparison to match the existing, methodology-grounded copy is a smaller, lower-risk change than rewording two independent copy sources (frontend MetricHelp + backend docstring) to match the code. Trade Grade's own threshold copy ('roughly 30%+') is already inclusive by its own wording, so it intentionally keeps the default `>=` behavior -- only the two 50%-anchored grades pass `strictlyAbove`.

decisions.decision: Extracted the shared sign-to-color three-way ternary into `frontend/src/utils/signColor.ts` (a plain `(theme, value) => string` function, not a hook or a new common/ component), and had both `common/PercentChange` and `common/SignedCurrency` call it.
decisions.rationale: A plain function (rather than a `useSignColor()` hook) keeps the call sites' existing `useTheme()` + one-line color derivation shape, needs no extra import of a hooks convention, and is trivially unit-testable on its own (added signColor.test.ts) without rendering a component. Placed under utils/ (alongside format.ts/chart.ts) rather than components/common/ since it renders nothing and has no props/story of its own -- it's a formatting-style utility, not a display component per Frontend.md's common/ vs utils/ distinction elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. formatCurrency).

decisions.decision: Marked TradeJournalPanel's buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct columns AND PositionsTable's pre-existing current_price column as `sortable: true`, removing the outdated 'DataTable's generic comparator has no defined ordering for a nullable percentage' comments from both.
decisions.rationale: DataTable's compareForSort operates on the raw `row[column.key]` value regardless of whether the column has a custom `render`, and already defines null-sorts-last ordering for exactly this nullable-number case (existing DataTable.test.tsx coverage). The checklist item explicitly flagged the PositionsTable precedent as worth revisiting too, since TradeJournalPanel's own (incorrect) comment had copied it; fixing only the newer copy would leave the same stale rationale on the older file it was copied from. Added a sort test to each panel confirming null-last ordering end to end (not just at the DataTable unit level).

comments.summary: Verified the 50%/30% threshold change against backend/app/portfolio/grading.py's own docstrings directly (not just the PR description): buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct say '>50% is "very good"' (strict), trade_grade_pct says '>=30% is an "A" trade' (inclusive). The PR's `strictlyAbove` prop applied to Buy Grade/Sell Grade only, with Trade Grade left on the default inclusive `>=`, matches exactly. Also cross-checked frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts's copy ('over 50%' vs 'Roughly 30%+') -- consistent.

signColor.ts extraction confirmed behavior-preserving by diffing both call sites (PercentChange.tsx, SignedCurrency.tsx) against the original inline ternary -- identical success/error/secondary mapping. Placement under frontend/src/utils/ (alongside format.ts) rather than components/common/ is correct per Frontend.md's common/-vs-utils distinction: it renders nothing, takes no props, has no story -- a plain (theme, value) => string helper, not a domain or presentational component.

Confirmed DataTable's compareForSort (frontend/src/components/common/DataTable/DataTable.tsx) sorts on the raw row value regardless of a column's custom render, and places null/undefined last unconditionally (not just in ascending direction). Verified live in a manual browser walkthrough (backend+frontend started with FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture) with real portfolio/trade-journal data: sorted PositionsTable by Current Price (one row null) and TradeJournalPanel by Buy Grade (one row's grades all null) in both directions -- the null row landed last every time, matching the docstring and this PR's claim.

Non-blocking: TradeJournalPanel.test.tsx's new 'sorts by a nullable grade column, missing values last' test doesn't actually include a null value in the sorted column (buy_grade_pct is 40/90 for both fixture rows; only the unsorted sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct are null). The test only verifies ordinary ascending sort, not the null-last behavior its name claims, unlike PositionsTable.test.tsx's equivalent test which does use a real null in the sorted column. Confirmed via live browser walkthrough that the actual null-last behavior is correct for TradeJournalPanel too, so this is a test-coverage/test-honesty gap, not a functional bug. Filed as docs/tasks/frontend-trade-journal-followups-followups.json.

review.notes: Full review: backend (807 tests, 99.92% coverage) and frontend (616 tests, 99.6%/98.9% line/branch coverage after re-running past one unrelated flaky timeout in PortfolioPage.test.tsx that passed in isolation and on a full re-run) both pass well above the 90% gate. ruff/mypy/eslint/`yarn tsc -b --noEmit` all clean. code-review skill (medium effort) found no correctness or reuse/simplification issues. Ran the persisted e2e suite (`make e2e`) -- all 16 specs across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist passed. This PR has no backend changes, so no OpenAPI snapshot check applies. No new frontend component was added (signColor.ts is a utility, not a component), so the frontend component-placement check (step 7a) doesn't apply beyond the utils/ placement already verified above. Did a live browser walkthrough (manually started backend+frontend with the fixture data provider, since no Playwright MCP tool was available in this session -- drove a headless Chromium instance directly via the frontend's own installed playwright-core package instead) covering: adding/deleting positions and closed trades, the trade-journal grade-cell bold/non-bold rendering at real (non-boundary) grade values matching the strict/inclusive threshold split, and sorting every newly-sortable column (Buy/Sell/Trade Grade, Current Price) in both directions including rows with null values. No console errors or failed network requests observed. One non-blocking test-coverage gap found and filed as a follow-up task; no blocking findings.
